title: Equip sales to sell it
summary: In business software, sales teams need to understand why a customer would buy, not just what the product does. Give them the story, the proof and the answers before launch.

beginner: Write one paragraph on who the product is for and why they would buy.
List the questions and objections customers are likely to raise, with answers.
Prepare a short demo that shows the main value.
Run a session with sales before launch and record it.
Ask sales a few weeks later what is missing.
intermediate: Work with product marketing on messaging, battlecards and demo scripts.
Brief customer success and support as well as sales.
Tell sales early about price changes or retired features.
experienced: Set a launch enablement standard across products.
Measure enablement by win rate and sales cycle, not attendance.
Bring sales feedback into product strategy.

toolExamples.confluence: Keep one sales page with the story, demo and answers.
toolExamples.notion: Keep a living list of objections and answers.

leaderView.good: Sales teams understand why a customer would buy, not just what the product does.
ask: Can sales explain the value in a customer's words?
signs: Sales promise features that don't exist.
Product never hears what loses deals.
